title: All In
description:
2 AM. The open group chat is exploding.

'If you don't buy this right now you'll regret it for life. It'll triple by tomorrow.'

Someone just posted they put in everything they had. The chart is going vertical.
There's money in the account right now.

Whether this opportunity is real or a trap — unknown.
But the window is right now.

choices.text: Stare at the chart. Close it.
choices.result_text: Closed the chat. Will find out the result in the morning. No idea if it was the right call.

title: The Startup Offer
description:
A message from a former colleague.

'Want to join our team? We just got seed funding. I'll give you equity.'

The company is six months old. No salary — stock options only.
Success means nine figures. Failure means unemployed.

Is there enough nerve to quit and jump in?

choices.text: Join them — quit the current job
choices.result_text: Put in the resignation. The account will drain fast. But if this works — everything changes.
Politely declined. Chose stability. No one knows how that friend's startup will turn out.
Agreed to join on weekends. Keep the day job, keep the option open.

title: The Gangnam Contact
description:
A conversation that started by chance in a Gangnam café.

The other person didn't give a name, but the way they spoke and dressed was different.
'There's an interesting project I'm working on. Looking for the right person to do it with.'

Opportunity or danger — impossible to read.
Chances like this may not come again.

choices.text: Hand over a card. Make an impression.
choices.result_text: Exchanged numbers. A week later, an invitation to a small gathering. The door to Gangnam opened slightly.

choices.text: Keep it light. Leave without giving contact info.
choices.result_text: Good conversation. But no contact exchanged. Never did learn their name.

title: Housing Lottery Win
description:
The long-forgotten청약 (housing subscription) account.

A text arrived. 'You have been selected in the public housing lottery.'

Hand trembled. A deposit is needed. Barely possible with current funds.

This is a real opportunity.

choices.text: Pay the deposit. Sign the contract.
choices.result_text: Stamped the contract. Move-in in two years. Hands wouldn't stop shaking. It didn't feel real — my own apartment.

choices.text: Can't cover the deposit right now. Pass.
choices.result_text: Sent the forfeit notice. Another chance will come someday. Someday.

title: Office Politics
description:
The team leader position opened up.

The general manager called {name} in quietly. 'You're the right fit. But Assistant Manager Kim is gunning for it too. What are you going to do?'

Playing it straight takes time.
Playing it politically is faster, but makes enemies.

Work, in the end, is a people game.

choices.text: Compete on merit. Let the work speak.
choices.result_text: Volunteered for overtime. Let results do the talking. It'll take time — but no regrets.

choices.text: Side with the GM. Play the politics.
choices.result_text: Got the team leader position. Salary went up. Assistant Manager Kim's eyes went cold. This industry — you take what comes with it.

choices.text: Pretend not to care. Start looking for other jobs.
choices.result_text: Stepped out of the race. Quietly opened a job listing site. Something better is out there.
